blockingFindings: Successful CLI review execution always fails its revision-binding check: revalidateCurrentReviewBinding is called with an object containing headSha/baseSha, but assertReviewRevisionUnchanged expects those fields on its first argument. Consequently valid successful reviews are rejected before review-bound persistence.
missingNegativeTests: Add an end-to-end regression proving a valid successful semantic review passes revision binding and persists its result.

architectureAssessment.deepModules: The launcher centralizes review binding, validation, cancellation, and persistence, but the broken binding-helper contract prevents the module from reliably fulfilling its boundary.
architectureAssessment.hexagonalArchitecture: Provider execution, review assessment, and repository evidence persistence remain separated conceptually; the current adapter integration is functionally blocked by the argument mismatch.
architectureAssessment.eventedBoundaries: Progress and terminal events are structured and fail-closed in design, but successful completion cannot reach the persistence boundary until revision validation is corrected.

exactNextAction: Correct the revalidateCurrentReviewBinding call or helper contract so the reviewed head/base object is validated against the current canonical revisions, then add and run a successful-review persistence regression before requesting fresh semantic review.
